div.div: i once debugged a wake stub at 2am. would do it again.
i have a bambu lab x1c and a problem with starting new projects
i think about edge cases in the shower
i like when things work reliably. so i make them work reliably.
i test things. sometimes before shipping.
started as a gaming fair volunteer. built a product instead.
one button on my stream deck deploys crewvolution to prod
i write firmware. also the backend. also the frontend.
if there's a PCB and a problem i'll be happy for weeks
every project starts with a folder and a dream
i told myself i'd keep it simple this time
maker by nature. engineer by necessity.
i speak microcontroller and server fluently
powered by energy drinks and a concerning amount of open tabs
if it's broken, i'm already fixing it
the LED blinks. we ship it.
i have more projects than hours in the day. working on both.
built crewvolution so gaming events could stop using excel
building the tools i wish existed
got tired of spreadsheets at gaming fairs
it compiles. mostly.
i automate things i could just do manually. it's a gift.
i care a lot about the things i make
i built a dev dashboard because i didn't like my other dev dashboards
streams are live. overlays are custom. send help.
added one more feature. and then one more. and then one more.
professionally unable to stop adding features
debugging is just detective work with worse coffee
i have a poker game running in docker. don't ask why.
the PCB is fine. probably.
i don't stop because i'm done. i stop because i'm tired.
maker. engineer. whatever it takes.
building an open-source robot arm. currently in pieces.
scope creep is a feature
CET/CEST. usually awake.
